title: Vocabulary: word forms and spelling for completion answers
status: Owner approved v1.1.0 on 2026-10-26; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional vocabulary lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional material, AI-assisted. Passages, people and data are fictional and created for practice. Not official IELTS material. Human editorial and classroom review recommended.
prerequisites: Lesson 3 (Listening details, spelling and word limits).
Learners know noun, verb, adjective and adverb.
Pitched at learners aiming for Band 6.5-7.5 who lose completion marks through spelling, plurals or the wrong word form.

objectives.text: Identify the word form a gap needs (noun, verb, adjective, adverb; singular or plural) from the grammar around it.
Find the exact form of a word in a passage when the question is paraphrased, and copy it accurately.
Spell high-frequency IELTS words correctly, including common traps (accommodation, environment, necessary).

levels.foundation: Keep the suffix list open; for each gap, write N, V, Adj or Adv before answering.
levels.core: Complete all tasks with the word bank closed after the word-family stage.
levels.extension: For each completion answer, name the clue word that shows the form (for example 'a' + adjective + noun).
levels.high_band: In the homework paragraph, use at least six different noun-forming or adjective-forming suffixes accurately.

word_bank.meaning: a place to stay (uncountable; double c, double m)
the natural world (note the n before m)
the group that rules a country (n before m)
word_bank.example: The government introduced a new law.
It is necessary to book in advance.

word_bank.meaning: a place for books / a place for experiments
environment → environmental; effect → effective; danger → dangerous; suffice → sufficient
a gap after 'several', 'many', 'two' needs a plural
no plural: information, equipment, advice, research, accommodation
sufficient → insufficient; possible → impossible; usual → unusual

stages.title: Opening challenge: right idea, lost mark
stages.student: Decide which answer would receive the mark.
stages.teacher: Learners vote; reveal the comments. Stress that IELTS marks spelling, number and form.
stages.say: The right idea in the wrong form scores zero.
stages.check: Learners say why Learner A and Learner C lose the mark.

stages.title: Word families and suffixes
stages.student: Complete a word-family table for five verbs from the bank (verb, noun, adjective, adverb).
stages.teacher: Board the suffix groups. Point out spelling changes (decide → decision, afford → affordability, suffice → sufficient).
stages.say: The suffix tells you the job of the word.

stages.title: Which form fits the gap?
stages.student: Choose the correct form. All four options are real words from the same family.
stages.teacher: Five minutes; reveal and ask for the clue word each time.
stages.say: Read the words before and after the gap.
stages.check: Learners name the clue for each answer.

stages.title: Reading: find the exact form
stages.student: Complete the notes with ONE word from the passage. The notes use different words, so find the idea first, then copy the exact form the gap needs.
stages.teacher: Eleven minutes, then reveal. Mark strictly: wrong form or spelling is wrong.
stages.say: Find the idea, check the form, copy the word exactly.
stages.check: Learners self-mark strictly and name the form of each answer.

stages.title: Listen and spell
stages.student: Read the form for 30 seconds, then listen once and complete it. Spelling must be correct.
stages.teacher: Read the script once at natural speed. Spell only the names that the script spells.
stages.say: Write, then use the last minute to check spelling, capitals and plurals.
stages.check: Most learners score five or more of seven.

stages.title: Spelling traps
stages.teacher: Quick-fire; learners copy the correct spellings into their notebooks.
stages.say: Learn the trap (double letter, silent letter), not just the word.
stages.check: Learners record their three hardest words.

stages.title: Error check
stages.student: Each sentence has ONE error of form, number or spelling. Write the correct word.
stages.teacher: Five minutes; reveal and classify each error (form, number, spelling).
stages.say: In the test, check every answer for these three errors.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and note the two homework tasks.
stages.say: Check every completion answer for form, number and spelling before you move on.
stages.check: Every learner spells five bank words correctly from memory.

blocks.title: Right idea, lost mark
blocks.mode: Opening challenge; learners decide before the reveal
blocks.instructions: Recording: '... we can offer accommodation for up to forty students.' Form: 'Type of help offered: ______ (ONE WORD)'. Three learners answered. Who gets the mark?

examples.label: Learner A
examples.comment: No mark: misspelt. 'Accommodation' has double c and double m.

examples.label: Learner B
examples.comment: Mark: correct word, correct spelling, one word.

examples.label: Learner C
examples.comment: No mark here: in British English 'accommodation' is normally uncountable, and the recording uses it without -s.

blocks.title: Which form fits the gap?
blocks.mode: Controlled practice; word bank closed for core and above
blocks.instructions: Choose the correct form, A, B, C or D, to complete each sentence. All the options are real words from the same word family.

items.prompt: The council has not yet made a final ______ about the new bridge.
items.reason: The article and adjective need a noun.

items.prompt: Cycling has grown in ______ over the last decade.
The new system is far more ______ than the old one.
items.reason: The comparative needs an adjective describing the system.

items.prompt: Prices increased ______ in the second half of the year.
items.reason: An adverb describes how prices increased.

items.prompt: There has been a marked ______ in air quality since the factory closed.
items.reason: The article and adjective need a noun.

items.prompt: Several ______ in the area were closed because of the storm.
items.evidence: several + plural noun (buildings that can be closed)
items.reason: 'Librarians' are people, who cannot be 'closed'; 'library' and 'librarian' are singular.

items.prompt: The new factory caused serious ______ damage to the river.
items.reason: An adjective describes 'damage'; 'environmentalist' refers to a person.

items.prompt: Researchers need more ______ before they can reach a conclusion.
items.reason: 'Information' is the noun; it has no plural.

blocks.title: Reading: find the exact form
blocks.mode: Timed practice under test-like conditions: eleven minutes, no dictionary
blocks.instructions: Complete the notes. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

stimulus.title: A new sports centre
paragraphs: The town's new sports centre, which opened in March after almost three years of construction, replaces a building that had become too expensive to maintain. It contains a twenty-five-metre swimming pool, two sports halls, a climbing wall and several outdoor courts. The architects were asked to minimise energy consumption, and the result is one of the most efficient public buildings in the region: solar panels on the roof generate around a third of its electricity, while rainwater collected from the roof is filtered and used in the toilets and changing rooms.

Accessibility was another priority. All entrances are at ground level, the pool has a moveable floor that can be raised for swimmers who need shallow water, and the changing rooms include several spaces designed for families and for people with disabilities. Local disability groups were consulted at an early stage, and several of their recommendations were adopted in the final design, including clearer signs, quieter hand dryers and a hoist to help wheelchair users into the pool.

Membership has exceeded expectations. Within six weeks of opening, more than two thousand residents had registered, and the management is now considering longer opening hours at weekends. The most popular facilities so far are the climbing wall and the evening yoga classes, which are frequently fully booked. To improve affordability, the council has introduced reduced prices for students, pensioners and people who are unemployed.

The centre has not been without criticism. Some residents complained that the car park, which has only eighty spaces, is insufficient for a building of this size, particularly on Saturday mornings when children's swimming lessons take place. The council responded by introducing a new bus route that stops outside the main entrance and by installing secure storage for more than a hundred bicycles.

Running the centre requires a team of around forty staff, including lifeguards, fitness instructors and cleaners, many of whom previously worked at the old building. The management has introduced a training programme so that all staff hold a recognised first-aid qualification, and several instructors have completed additional courses in teaching swimming to adults, a service for which there has been unexpectedly strong demand. Local schools also use the pool on weekday mornings, an arrangement that provides the centre with a reliable income during hours when few adult members visit.

Others questioned the decision to demolish the old building rather than renovate it. The council argued that renovation would have cost almost as much as a new building while producing a centre that was far less efficient. Independent engineers who reviewed the plans broadly supported this conclusion, although they noted that the demolition itself had generated a considerable amount of waste, much of which could not be recycled.

items.prompt: Design goal: keep the building's use of energy, or its energy ______, as low as possible.
items.evidence: The architects were asked to minimise energy consumption
items.reason: Noun after 'energy'; 'minimise' = keep as low as possible.

items.prompt: Power: about a third of the centre's ______ is produced on top of the building.
items.evidence: solar panels on the roof generate around a third of its electricity
items.reason: 'Produced on top of the building' paraphrases 'generate ... on the roof'.

items.prompt: Water: ______ is cleaned and reused in toilets and changing rooms.
items.evidence: rainwater collected from the roof is filtered and used in the toilets and changing rooms

items.prompt: Design input: some ______ from local disability groups were included in the plans.
items.evidence: several of their recommendations were adopted in the final design

items.prompt: Most popular so far: the climbing wall and evening ______ sessions.
items.evidence: the climbing wall and the evening yoga classes

items.prompt: To increase the centre's ______, cheaper prices are offered to some groups.
items.evidence: To improve affordability, the council has introduced reduced prices
items.reason: The possessive 'the centre's' needs a noun; 'affordable' is the adjective.

items.prompt: Criticism: the parking provided is ______ on busy days.
items.evidence: the car park, which has only eighty spaces, is insufficient for a building of this size
items.reason: After 'is', the gap needs an adjective meaning 'not enough'.

items.prompt: Old building: ______ was rejected because it would have cost nearly as much as a new centre.
items.evidence: renovation would have cost almost as much as a new building
items.reason: The subject of the sentence needs a noun; 'renovate' is the verb.

blocks.instructions: Listen and complete the booking form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

stimulus.title: Booking a study room
paragraphs: RECEPTIONIST: Good morning, Riverside College library. How can I help?
STUDENT: Hello, I'd like to book a study room for a group project. My surname is Whitfield, that's W-H-I-T-F-I-E-L-D.
RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. Which day would you like?
STUDENT: Wednesday, please, the fourteenth of February, in the afternoon.
RECEPTIONIST: Fine. All our rooms have whiteboards, and you can borrow a projector, but please note that food is not allowed. Will you need any equipment?
STUDENT: Just the projector, thanks. Oh, and is it necessary to bring a student card?
RECEPTIONIST: Yes, you'll need it to enter the building after six o'clock. The room is on the third floor, next to the laboratory, not the library entrance, so take the lift on the left.

items.prompt: Surname: ______
items.reason: Spelt in the recording; capital letter.

items.prompt: Equipment to borrow: ______
Not allowed in rooms: ______
Student card needed after: ______ p.m.
items.evidence: you'll need it to enter the building after six o'clock

items.prompt: Location: third floor, next to the ______
items.evidence: next to the laboratory, not the library entrance

blocks.title: Homework: word families in use
blocks.mode: Homework; checked at the start of the next lesson
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-3: Write the noun form of each word (ONE word). Questions 4-6: Rewrite each sentence using the word in brackets in the correct form. Keep the meaning the same.

items.prompt: responsible → ______
explain → ______
describe → ______
Rewrite: 'The council decided to close the pool.' (decision)
items.answer: The council made the decision to close the pool.
items.reason: Accept 'made a/the decision to' or 'The council's decision was to close the pool.'

items.prompt: Rewrite: 'Cycling has become much more popular.' (popularity)
items.answer: There has been a significant rise in the popularity of cycling.
items.reason: Accept any accurate sentence using the noun 'popularity'.

items.prompt: Rewrite: 'The new rules were effective in reducing noise.' (effectively)
items.answer: The new rules effectively reduced noise.
items.reason: Accept any accurate sentence using the adverb correctly.

blocks.title: Homework: describe a public facility
blocks.mode: Homework; teacher feedback on word form, spelling and accuracy
blocks.prompt: Write a paragraph of about 130 words describing a public facility in your town or city (for example a library, park, pool or station). Explain what it offers and one way it could be improved. Underline every noun ending in -tion, -ment or -ity and every adjective ending in -al, -ive or -ient that you use.
blocks.conditions: 20 minutes, without a dictionary, translator or AI tool. Write the start and finish time, then check every underlined word for spelling and form.
blocks.support: Useful forms: facility/facilities, accessible/accessibility, improve/improvement, popular/popularity, environment/environmental, sufficient/insufficient.
blocks.extension: Use at least one negative adjective (insufficient, inaccessible, unreliable).
blocks.high_band: Use six different suffixes accurately without forcing them.
blocks.model_label: Illustrative model for teacher feedback only. Not a certified band answer.
blocks.model: The central library in my city is one of its most popular public facilities. Since its renovation three years ago, it has offered a quiet reading room, free internet access and a collection of more than fifty thousand books. Its accessibility has also improved considerably: there is now a lift to every floor and a ramp at the main entrance. However, the opening hours are insufficient for many students, because the building closes at six o'clock on weekdays, just when most people finish work or school. In my view, the most effective improvement would be to extend the evening opening hours, even if only on two days a week. This relatively small change would make the library far more useful to the people who depend on it most.
checklist: Word form: Is every underlined word the correct part of speech for its position?
Spelling: Are double letters and silent letters correct?
Number: Are plurals and uncountable nouns used correctly?
Task: Does the paragraph describe the facility and suggest one improvement?

exit_ticket: Three words I will now spell correctly:
The clue that tells me a gap needs a noun:
One word family I can write in full (verb, noun, adjective, adverb):
homework: Write the paragraph about a public facility and check every underlined word.

stimulus.title: Joining a community choir
paragraphs: ORGANISER: Thanks for calling the Hillview Community Choir. Rehearsals are on Thursday evenings in the old town hall.
CALLER: Do I need any experience?
ORGANISER: No, but beginners usually attend two introductory sessions first. The membership fee covers the cost of sheet music and the hire of the hall.
CALLER: And what should I bring?

ORGANISER: Just a pencil and a bottle of water. Oh, and we're looking for volunteers to help with publicity for our spring concert, which will raise money for the local hospital. If you're interested, please contact our secretary, Mrs Coutts, that's C-O-U-T-T-S.

blocks.title: Fresh check: which form fits?
blocks.instructions: Choose the correct form, A, B, C or D, to complete each sentence.

items.prompt: There has been a steady ______ in the number of tourists.
items.reason: The article and adjective need a noun.

items.prompt: The bridge was closed for ______ reasons.
items.evidence: noun used before another noun: safety reasons
items.reason: The fixed phrase is 'for safety reasons'; 'safe reasons' would mean the reasons are safe, and 'safely' and 'saves' cannot describe a noun.

items.prompt: Public transport in the area is ______; buses are often late or cancelled.
items.reason: The explanation shows a negative meaning: 'unreliable'.

items.prompt: Several new sports ______ have been built near the station.
items.reason: 'Facility' is singular; 'facilitate' is a verb; a 'facilitator' is a person, who cannot be built.
